clue.text: Demanding thin porridge with fish

parts.note: gruel is a thin, watery porridge of oats boiled in water or milk
the ling is a long-bodied food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone is hard to please, insisting on watery porridge served with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demanding' looks like a verb describing a fussy diner, but it is the adjective meaning exhausting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a task that is exhausting and requires great effort, as in a tough schedule.

clue.text: Heartless girl has friends from across the channel at the castle

indicators.note: taking the heart out of the word girl leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: amis is the French for friends, and France lies across the English Channel from Britain

explanation.surface: A girl with French friends is staying at a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: GLAMIS is a castle in Scotland, the childhood home of the late Queen Mother and the setting of Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamis is a historic Scottish fortress, in Angus, linked with Shakespeare's Macbeth.

clue.text: In default I'm a tallyman accepting the last offers

indicators.note: the letters wanted lie inside the run of words default I'm a tallyman

explanation.surface: Someone in arrears with a door-to-door debt collector takes the final terms offered.
explanation.walkthrough: A tallyman is a British door-to-door collector of instalment payments; 'accepting' is a link word joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Latin word for a final demand or offer that will not be bettered, the terms given before negotiation ends.

clue.text: Ambulance did come round when someone had been speared

indicators.note: the words Ambulance did come round, or enclose, the letters wanted, running across both words

explanation.surface: An ambulance arrived after someone had been run through with a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come round' looks like part of the emergency scene, but it says the two words before it surround the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to pierce with a pointed weapon or blade, so the past form matches pierced with a spear.

clue.text: I demonstrated chemical

parts.note: protesters who occupy a place in protest have staged a sit-in, so they sat in

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having demonstrated a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstrated' reads as showing something off, but here it means protested by occupying a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Isatin is an orange-red organic compound used in making dyes such as indigo.

clue.text: Half narcotic drug removed from wine

indicators.note: removed here means shifted out of place, so the letters are rearranged into a new order
only the front half of the word narcotic is used, its first four letters

explanation.surface: Half a narcotic drug has been taken out of a wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' reads as taken away, but it means moved again: NARC (half of 'narcotic') plus DRUG is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand cru is the French classification for a top-ranked vineyard or the fine vintage it produces.

clue.text: Sarah in charge? Not according to this law

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of the name Sarah

explanation.surface: Could a woman called Sarah be put in charge? This law says not.
explanation.walkthrough: The Salic law, from the Frankish code, barred women from inheriting the throne, so a Sarah could never be in charge under it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salic code excluded females from succession to the crown, so a woman ruling breaks that rule.

clue.text: It is thoughtful to put you and me beneath workroom

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set beneath another is written after it

parts.note: a studio is a room where an artist or craftsperson works
us is the pronoun covering you and me together

explanation.surface: Someone reflective tells you and me to go downstairs below the workroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Being devoted to reading and learning makes a person reflective and given to contemplation.

clue.text: Story, finish first stage

indicators.note: first says the word for stage comes ahead of the word for finish

parts.note: a leg is one stage of a journey or race
the end of something is its finish

explanation.surface: A tale of someone completing the opening stage of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first stage' looks like one phrase, but 'first' is placing the piece from 'stage' before the piece from 'finish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale, often of heroes, handed down from the past.

clue.text: Near race that is fiercely contested

parts.note: close means near in distance
a run is a race on foot

explanation.surface: A race that is nearly level is hard fought.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-run contest is one won by only a narrow margin, decided after a hard struggle.

clue.text: In the ocean ten navigators needed aerial

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit inside the run of words the ocean ten navigators

explanation.surface: Sailors crossing the ocean need a radio aerial to find their way.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial is the rod or wire that receives or sends radio signals, the same device under another name.

clue.text: Camping clothing?

parts.note: the reading is a garment for a campsite, but the real sense is a loose, flared frock shaped like a canvas shelter

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this is not gear for a campsite but a style of garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose dress that widens from the shoulders to the hem, like the outline of a canvas shelter.

clue.text: Substitute's unending reputation

indicators.note: unending says the last letter of the word for reputation is cut off

parts.note: standing is a person's status or reputation

explanation.surface: A replacement player's reputation never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Substitute's' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a person who takes another's place, a replacement or understudy.

clue.text: Key to how the German made soup

parts.note: C is a musical key
der is the German masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the secret was to how a German cook made a soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a secret, but it is the musical key C.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick, creamy soup, typically made with clams or fish.

clue.text: Who is in the van?

parts.note: read as a question about a vehicle's occupant, but being in the van means being in front, and the clue itself is a question that leads

explanation.walkthrough: 'in the van' means in the vanguard, at the front; a question that steers the answer is the real sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A query framed to prompt the reply the asker wants, as a barrister might put to a witness.

clue.text: Saw cat on top that's sharp-sighted

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece on top is written first

parts.note: the lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears
to have eyed something is to have seen or looked at it

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a cat on the roof that has keen vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the start of a sentence about seeing, and is: it means looked at.
explanation.definitionFit: Having keen vision, from the old belief that the wild cat could see through walls.

clue.text: I am put to the test, that's better

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
to prove something is to test it, as a gun is proved

explanation.surface: Someone tested says they feel better now.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made better has been enhanced or developed.

clue.text: Reported Gary and junior at fortified place

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the clue words are heard, not written

parts.note: Gary plus son, since a junior is a son named after his father

explanation.surface: Gary and his son are said to be at a fort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junior' gives SON, so 'Gary's son' said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a fortified post where troops are stationed.

clue.text: One cannot get off with it

definitions.text: One cannot get off with it

parts.words: One cannot get off with it
parts.note: read as a failed romance, but get off here means fall asleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'get off' is British for drop off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is a chronic inability to sleep.

clue.text: Poor hen out of place, it has absolutely nil chance of success

definitions.text: it has absolutely nil chance of success

indicators.note: the letters of poor hen are set out of their place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sickly hen in the wrong spot has absolutely no chance of success.
explanation.definitionFit: Somebody with no prospect of winning, a hopeless case, in Australian and British slang.

clue.text: Connect bent piece of metal completely

parts.note: a hook is a bent or curved piece of metal used for hanging things
up can mean completely, as in eat up or use up

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fully attach a bent piece of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To hook up is to link one device to another.

clue.text: Party at joint, have a drink

parts.note: the knee is the joint in the leg
to sup is to sip or drink

explanation.surface: At a party, someone sips a drink at a pub, a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is a lively British party; 'joint' looks like a bar, but it is the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: A boisterous, lively celebration with dancing, a British informal term.

clue.text: Vehicle put together by amateur carrier of equipment

indicators.note: carrier of equipment means a carrier for kit, so kit comes first

parts.note: kit is equipment
a car is a vehicle that carries people

explanation.surface: An amateur builds a vehicle to carry equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A car bought as parts and assembled by a hobbyist rather than a factory.

clue.text: One hug could be sufficient

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of one hug could become another word

explanation.surface: A single embrace might be all that is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate, as much as is needed.

clue.text: Appealed to the highest authority

parts.note: read as a legal case taken to the top court, but the highest authority is God

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a court case going upward, but the authority is divine.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray is to make a request to God.

clue.text: Changes to incomes he can explain?

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of to incomes are reordered

explanation.surface: An expert in money matters can explain shifts in incomes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' is the anagram signal for TO INCOMES; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert in the production and distribution of wealth could explain how earnings shift.

clue.text: Composed tune in churchyard about spicy relish

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the word for churchyard

parts.note: CH is church and Y yard, so churchyard gives CH and Y

indicators.note: composed suggests putting the letters of tune into a new order

explanation.surface: A tune written in a churchyard about a spicy relish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' reads as a description of the tune, but it is the anagram signal; 'about' is only a link. Y is a recognised abbreviation for yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangy condiment made from fruit, vinegar and spices.

clue.text: Ineffective person going round gym was deceived

indicators.note: going round says the word for useless person surrounds the word for gym

parts.note: a dud is a useless or ineffective person or thing
PE, physical education, is gym class

explanation.surface: An ineffective person going round a gym was tricked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ineffective person' sounds like a description of a gym-goer, but it is the outer piece, with 'going round' telling it to enclose the gym abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been tricked or fooled.

clue.text: Up on the map?

parts.note: read as being shown on a map, but up on a map is the direction toward the top

explanation.walkthrough: Maps are drawn with north at the top, so going up the page means heading toward the pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading toward the pole, which sits at the top of a conventional map.
